title: Priceable Entity
requirement:
[p83]       2.1.     DATA-001 Priceable Entity
[p83] 
[p83] 
[p83] The workspace must support the creation and management of Priceable Entities.
[p83] 
[p83] A Priceable Entity is a business offering to which the organisation can assign or evaluate a
[p83] distinct selling price within an applicable pricing context.
[p83] 
[p83] Supported Priceable Entity types must include, at minimum:
[p83] 
[p83]     ● product;
[p83]     ● SKU or product variant;
[p83]     ● service;
[p83]     ● another organisation-defined directly priceable offering.
[p83] 
[p83] A product may itself be a Priceable Entity where the organisation prices that product directly.
[p83] 
[p83] Where individual SKUs or variants of a product have distinct selling prices, each
[p83] independently priced SKU or variant must be represented as its own Priceable Entity.
[p83] 
[p83] Categories and product groups must not become Priceable Entities solely because they are
[p83] used to organise, filter or apply pricing work across multiple Priceable Entities.
[p83] 
[p83] Pricing dimensions such as location, region, channel, customer group, business unit, vendor
[p83] or price list must remain distinct from the Priceable Entity itself.
[p83] 
[p83] A Priceable Entity may therefore have different Price Records, Cost Records or pricing
[p83] outcomes across supported pricing dimensions without becoming a different Priceable Entity
[p83] unless the organisation's underlying commercial object is itself different.
[p83] 
[p83] Each Priceable Entity must have, at minimum:
[p83] 
[p83]     ● unique Owómidé identifier;
[p83]     ● organisation-defined name;
[p83]     ● entity type;
[p83] 
[p84]       ● status.
[p84] 
[p84] Where available, a Priceable Entity may also contain:
[p84] 
[p84]       ● SKU, product code or external identifier;
[p84]       ● parent product or related organisational grouping;
[p84]       ● category;
[p84]       ● brand;
[p84]       ● base unit of measure;
[p84]       ● description;
[p84]       ● organisation-specific reference fields.
[p84] 
[p84] Currency must be associated with the applicable monetary record or pricing context rather
[p84] than assumed to be an immutable property of the Priceable Entity.
[p84] 
[p84] The Priceable Entity model must remain sufficiently flexible to support organisations that
[p84] price at product, SKU, variant or service level without requiring every organisation to use the
[p84] same catalogue hierarchy.
[p84] 
[p84]

title: Price Record and Current Price
requirement:
[p84]         2.3.      DATA-003 Price Record and Current Price
[p84] 
[p84] 
[p84] The system must allow an organisation to maintain structured Price Records for Priceable
[p84] Entities.
[p84] 
[p85] A Price Record represents a selling-price value for a Priceable Entity within a defined pricing
[p85] context.
[p85] 
[p85] Each Price Record must identify, where applicable:
[p85] 
[p85]    ● Priceable Entity;
[p85]    ● price amount;
[p85]    ● currency;
[p85]    ● applicable pricing dimensions;
[p85]    ● effective-from date or timestamp;
[p85]    ● effective-to date or timestamp where applicable;
[p85]    ● source;
[p85]    ● last updated timestamp.
[p85] 
[p85] The system must support different Price Records for the same Priceable Entity where pricing
[p85] legitimately differs by location, channel, customer group, price list, currency or another
[p85] configured pricing dimension.
[p85] 
[p85] The system must also preserve multiple Price Records over time for the same pricing
[p85] context where the selling price changes.
[p85] 
[p85] Current Price means the specific Price Record that is presently applicable to a Priceable
[p85] Entity within the relevant pricing context at the applicable reference time.
[p85] 
[p85] A Current Price must therefore remain associated with:
[p85] 
[p85]    ● the Priceable Entity;
[p85]    ● price amount;
[p85]    ● currency;
[p85]    ● applicable pricing dimensions;
[p85]    ● effective context;
[p85]    ● source Price Record.
[p85] 
[p85] The system must not silently treat the newest Price Record, most recently imported value or
[p85] another arbitrary Price Record as the Current Price where more than one record could apply.
[p85] 
[p85] For the same Priceable Entity and exact pricing context, the system must not represent
[p85] conflicting Price Records as simultaneously being the Current Price for the same reference
[p85] time.
[p85] 
[p86] Where overlapping, conflicting or insufficiently specified Price Records prevent the Current
[p86] Price from being determined unambiguously, the system must identify the Current Price as
[p86] unresolved and require appropriate authorised correction or selection rather than silently
[p86] choosing a value.
[p86] 
[p86] A future-effective Price Record must not become Current Price before its applicable effective
[p86] time.
[p86] 
[p86] A historical Price Record must remain preserved after it ceases to be Current Price.
[p86] 
[p86] Where no applicable Price Record exists, Current Price must be represented as unavailable
[p86] rather than assumed to be zero or inferred from another pricing context.
[p86] 
[p86] Any consequential pricing work that uses Current Price must remain traceable to the exact
[p86] Price Record and pricing context from which that Current Price was determined.
[p86] 
[p86]

title: Cost Record and Applicable Unit Cost
requirement:
[p86]         2.4.   DATA-004 Cost Record and Applicable Unit Cost
[p86] 
[p86] 
[p86] Where cost information is available, the MVP must allow authorised users to maintain
[p86] structured Cost Records for priceable entities.
[p86] 
[p86] A Cost Record represents an organisation-supplied or externally sourced cost value. It must
[p86] not be assumed to represent a universal accounting definition of cost.
[p86] 
[p86] Each Cost Record must identify, where applicable:
[p86] 
[p86]    ● affected priceable entity;
[p86]    ● cost amount;
[p86]    ● currency;
[p86]    ● unit of measure or cost unit;
[p86]    ● cost basis;
[p86]    ● applicable pricing dimensions;
[p86]    ● effective date or effective period;
[p86]    ● source;
[p86]    ● last updated timestamp.
[p86] 
[p86] Cost basis must identify what the cost value represents. Supported cost bases may include:
[p86] 
[p86]    ● acquisition or purchase cost;
[p86]    ● landed cost;
[p86] 
[p87]    ● production or manufacturing cost;
[p87]    ● direct service-delivery cost;
[p87]    ● another organisation-defined cost basis.
[p87] 
[p87] The MVP must allow more than one Cost Record to exist for the same priceable entity where
[p87] the records represent different cost bases, pricing dimensions or effective periods.
[p87] 
[p87] Owómidé must not silently treat the newest Cost Record, an average historical cost or any
[p87] particular cost basis as the correct cost for every pricing decision.
[p87] 
[p87] For every deterministic pricing calculation that requires cost, the system must identify the
[p87] Applicable Unit Cost used by that calculation.
[p87] 
[p87] Applicable Unit Cost means the specific cost value and cost basis selected for the relevant
[p87] pricing context and expressed on a unit basis compatible with the selling price being
[p87] analysed.
[p87] 
[p87] The Applicable Unit Cost must be traceable to either:
[p87] 
[p87]    ● a structured Cost Record; or
[p87]    ● an explicit assumed cost permitted under the applicable assumption requirements.
[p87] 
[p87] The calculation context must preserve enough information to identify:
[p87] 
[p87]    ● cost amount used;
[p87]    ● cost basis used;
[p87]    ● currency;
[p87]    ● applicable unit of measure;
[p87]    ● applicable pricing dimensions;
[p87]    ● source Cost Record or explicit assumption;
[p87]    ● effective context relevant to the pricing decision.
[p87] 
[p87] Where multiple potentially applicable Cost Records exist and the correct cost basis cannot
[p87] be determined from the pricing context or organisation configuration, the system must
[p87] require an authorised user to identify the applicable cost rather than selecting one silently.
[p87] 
[p87] Where a cost cannot be expressed on a unit basis compatible with the selling price, the
[p87] system must not use that value directly in gross-profit, gross-margin, markup or target-price
[p87] calculations.
[p87] 
[p88] The MVP is not required to operate as a full cost-accounting system, perform
[p88] enterprise-wide overhead allocation or independently construct accounting cost values from
[p88] incomplete source data.
[p88] 
[p88] Changes to cost information over time must create or preserve historical cost context rather
[p88] than overwriting the cost basis used in earlier consequential pricing work.
[p88] 
[p88]

[p104]     ● an initiative must not enter Completed until applicable completion conditions are

[p130]       5.4.     ANALYSIS-004 Gross Margin and Target-Margin Price Calculation
[p130] 
[p130] 
[p130] Where the selling price and the Applicable Unit Cost defined in DATA-004 are available, the
[p130] gross margin percentage must be calculated as:
[p130] 
[p130] Gross Margin % = ((Selling Price - Applicable Unit Cost) / Selling Price) × 100
[p130] 
[p130] This calculation is valid only where Selling Price is greater than zero.
[p130] 
[p130] The system must distinguish gross margin from markup.
[p130] 
[p130] Where a user defines a target gross-margin percentage and the Applicable Unit Cost defined
[p130] in DATA-004 is available and greater than zero, the system must deterministically derive the
[p130] corresponding proposed selling price as:
[p130] 
[p130] Proposed Selling Price = Applicable Unit Cost / (1 - (Target Gross Margin % / 100))
[p130] 
[p131] The target gross-margin percentage used in this calculation must be less than 100%.
[p131] 
[p131] Where the target gross-margin percentage is equal to or greater than 100%, or the required
[p131] Applicable Unit Cost is unavailable or invalid, the system must not produce a derived
[p131] proposed selling price and must identify why the calculation cannot be completed.
[p131] 
[p131] Where organisational policy permits a negative target gross margin, the calculation may
[p131] proceed provided the required inputs are valid and the resulting price satisfies applicable
[p131] guardrails.
[p131] 
[p131] The system must preserve the Applicable Unit Cost, cost basis, source Cost Record or
[p131] explicit cost assumption, target gross-margin percentage, formula and resulting unrounded
[p131] proposed selling price used in the calculation.
[p131]

title: Price Adjustment and Price Change Calculation
requirement:
[p132]       5.6.    ANALYSIS-006 Price Adjustment and Price Change Calculation
[p132] 
[p132] 
[p132] Where a pricing action derives a proposed selling price from a baseline price, the baseline
[p132] used by the calculation must be explicitly identifiable.
[p132] 
[p132] The baseline may be the current selling price or another supported pricing baseline explicitly
[p132] defined by the pricing action.
[p132] 
[p132] Where the baseline is Current Price, the calculation must use the Current Price defined in
[p132] DATA-003 for the affected Priceable Entity and pricing context.
[p132] 
[p132] Where no unambiguous Current Price exists, the system must not silently select another
[p132] Price Record as Current Price.
[p132] 
[p132] An authorised user may define another supported pricing baseline where the pricing action
[p132] permits it, but that baseline must remain explicitly distinguishable from Current Price.
[p132] 
[p132] Where:
[p132] 
[p132] Baseline Price = B
[p132] 
[p132] Percentage Adjustment = R
[p132] 
[p132] Absolute Adjustment = A
[p132] 
[p132] the MVP must support the following deterministic calculations where applicable.
[p132] 
[p132] For a percentage increase:
[p132] 
[p132] Proposed Selling Price = B × (1 + (R / 100))
[p132] 
[p133] For a percentage decrease:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B × (1 - (R / 100))
[p133] 
[p133] For an absolute-value increase:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B + A
[p133] 
[p133] For an absolute-value decrease:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B - A
[p133] 
[p133] For promotional, discount or markdown pricing expressed as a percentage reduction:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B × (1 - (Discount % / 100))
[p133] 
[p133] For promotional, discount or markdown pricing expressed as an absolute-value reduction:
[p133] 
[p133] Proposed Selling Price = B - Discount Amount
[p133] 
[p133] Percentage reductions must not be less than 0% or greater than 100%.
[p133] 
[p133] Absolute reductions must not produce a negative proposed selling price.
[p133] 
[p133] Where a promotional, markdown or other pricing action directly specifies the final selling
[p133] price rather than an adjustment, that value must be treated as the proposed selling price
[p133] rather than recalculated through an adjustment formula.
[p133] 
[p133] After the proposed selling price is determined, the system must calculate price change
[p133] against Current Price where an unambiguous Current Price is available under DATA-003.
[p133] 
[p133] Where Current Price is available:
[p133] 
[p133] Absolute Price Change = Proposed Price - Current Price
[p133] 
[p133] and, where Current Price is not zero:
[p133] 
[p133] Price Change % = ((Proposed Price - Current Price) / Current Price) × 100
[p133] 
[p133] Where Current Price is zero, percentage price change must be represented as unavailable
[p133] rather than producing an undefined or misleading percentage.
[p133] 
[p133] Where Current Price is unavailable or unresolved, absolute and percentage change against
[p133] Current Price must be represented as unavailable.
[p133] 
[p134] Unavailability of Current Price must not prevent a pricing action from being deterministically
[p134] calculated where that action validly uses another explicitly identified pricing baseline and all
[p134] inputs required for that calculation are available.
[p134] 
[p134] Where the product displays a change relative to an alternative pricing baseline, that result
[p134] must be explicitly identified as change relative to that baseline and must not be labelled as
[p134] change from Current Price.
[p134] 
[p134] The system must preserve the pricing action, baseline value, baseline type, adjustment
[p134] value, calculation method and resulting proposed selling price used in the calculation.
[p134] 
[p134] Where Current Price is the baseline, the preserved calculation context must remain
[p134] traceable to the exact source Price Record defined under DATA-003.
[p134] 
[p134]

title: Analytical Completeness for Proposal Preparation
requirement:
[p144]     5.26.     ANALYSIS-026 Analytical Completeness for Proposal Preparation
[p144] 
[p144] 
[p144] Before analysed pricing work is used to prepare a formal Pricing Proposal, the analytical
[p144] layer must determine whether the decision-relevant analysis is sufficiently complete to
[p144] support Proposal preparation.
[p144] 
[p144] The analytical completeness check must identify, where applicable:
[p144] 
[p144]    ● unresolved calculation errors;
[p144]    ● missing required financial inputs;
[p144]    ● calculations that remain unavailable;
[p144]    ● invalid pricing outputs;
[p144]    ● material assumptions that are undefined or insufficiently identified;
[p144]    ● applicable Guardrails that remain Unable to Evaluate because required analytical
[p144]        information is missing or invalid.
[p144] 
[p144] A Guardrail Breach is an analytical evaluation result and must not automatically be
[p144] represented as an analytical error.
[p144] 
[p144] The governance consequence of a Guardrail Breach is determined by the configured
[p144] behavioural treatment under GOV-025.
[p144] 
[p145] The analytical layer must not independently determine whether a Pricing Proposal may be
[p145] submitted.
[p145] 
[p145] Formal Proposal submission readiness, including treatment of Warning, Approval Escalation,
[p145] Blocking and Unable to Evaluate Guardrail results, is governed by PROP-009.
[p145] 
[p145] Analytical completeness must therefore supply authoritative analysis and Guardrail
[p145] evaluation information to Proposal readiness without becoming a second owner of
[p145] submission policy.
[p145] 
[p145]

[p146]      5.30.    ANALYSIS-030 Analytical Completeness Principle
[p146] 
[p146] 
[p146] The MVP must provide enough analytical capability for a pricing team to determine:
[p146] 
[p146] What is the current economic position?
[p146] What are we proposing to change?
[p146] What does that change do to the economics?
[p146] Which assumptions are we relying on?
[p146] Which guardrails are affected?
[p146] What alternatives were considered?
[p146] 
[p146] If those questions cannot be answered from the Pricing Initiative before submission, the
[p146] pricing work is not decision-ready.

[p148] 3.6 Pricing Proposal Management
[p148] 
[p149]                        6. PRICING PROPOSAL MANAGEMENT
[p149] The Pricing Proposal is the formal decision object through which developed pricing work is
[p149] presented for organisational review, approval or policy authorisation.
[p149] 
[p149] A Pricing Proposal must represent the specific pricing action the organisation is being asked
[p149] to decide on. It must remain distinct from the broader Pricing Initiative, exploratory Scenarios
[p149] and editable working material inside the Pricing Builder.
[p149] 
[p149] The MVP must preserve a clear relationship between:
[p149] 
[p149] Pricing Initiative → Pricing Work and Analysis → Pricing Proposal → Organisational
[p149] Decision → Execution
[p149] 
[p149] The Pricing Initiative remains the primary container for the complete body of pricing work.
[p149] The Pricing Proposal represents the exact action submitted for decision.
[p149]
